elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate" (mutual, so available to Client; the "financially responsible" qualifier is a minor shortfall to note only)

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "No such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights ... without the prior written approval of the other party"

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Client's approval of any assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "no change of control of Client shall give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: successor carve-out runs only one way: "an assignment by Client to a successor"
no notice mechanic appears in the inserted sentence

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: reasonableness applies only to "Client's approval of any assignment by TrueLink", not to TrueLink's approval of Client assignments

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are present: affiliate carve-out (retained from the original mutual language), Client successor carve-out, Vendor consent requirement, reasonableness standard on our consent, competitor bar on Vendor assignment, and no Vendor termination right on Client change of control.

The edit is a single concise insertion that leaves the existing mutual consent requirement and affiliate carve-out intact; no clause rewrite, no new exceptions, no undefined terms or dangling mechanics.

Fallback is not independently satisfied (one-way successor right, no written-notice mechanic, reasonableness only on Client's consent), but the locked target is preferred and the preferred bargain is complete, so this is immaterial.

Minor note only: the retained affiliate carve-out is qualified by "financially responsible", a narrower condition than the preferred unqualified affiliate right; flag in rationale, not as a deviation.
